question: Two towns $A$ and $B$ are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every $T$ minutes. question: What is the nature of the graph between momentum of a body and its kinetic energy?

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let the mass of the body be $m$ and velocity of the body be $v$ , such that it has momentum $p$ and kinetic energy E. Momentum, $p=m v$ $\Rightarrow p^{2}=m^{2} v^{2}$ Kinetic energy, $E=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}$ $\Rightarrow E=\frac{p^{2}}{2 m}$ Hence, the nature of the graph between momentum of a body and its kinetic energy is parabola. i,e., $E \propto p^{2}$ © examsnet.com

subject: Physics
question: A uniform disc of radius ' $a$ ' and mass ' $m$ ' is rotating freely with an angular speed of ' $\omega$ ' in a horizontal plane about a smooth fixed vertical axis passing through its center. A particle, also of mass ' $m$ ' is suddenly attached to the rim of the disc and starts to rotate with it. The new angular speed of this system is ______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given, mass of disc $=m$ Radius of disc $=a$ Angular speed $=\omega$ Moment of inertia of the disc, $I=\frac{1}{2} m a^{2}$ Initial angular momentum, $L_{i}=I \times \omega = \frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega$ Let $\omega'$ be the angular momentum of the disc when the particle of mass $m$ is attached at the rim. Final angular momentum, $L_{f}=I \omega' + m a v'$ $=\frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega' + m a^{2} \omega'$ $[\therefore v' = \omega' a]$ Applying conservation of angular momentum, $L_{i}=L_{f}$ $\frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega = \frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega' + m a^{2} \omega'$ $\Rightarrow \omega' = \frac{\omega}{3}$ © examsnet.com
transcription_status: published educational transcription; original PDF remains authoritative

question: Match the following entries in column-I and column-II with respect to an oscillating spring-block system: Column-I Column-II (a) Mass of the block is doubled (i) Energy of oscillation becomes 4 times (b) Spring constant is made 4 times (ii) Speed of block becomes 2 times (c) Amplitude of oscillations is doubled (iii) P.E. becomes 4 times (d) Angular frequency is doubled (iv) Time period becomes $\sqrt{\sqrt{2}}$ times

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: (A) Time-period in spring-block system is given by, $T=2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$ If mass is doubled, $T'=2\pi \sqrt{\frac{2m}{k}}$ ⇒ $T'=\sqrt{2} T$ Hence, time period becomes $\sqrt{2}$ times, if the mass of the block is doubled. $(A \rightarrow 4)$ (B) For spring, $PE=\frac{1}{2} k x^{2}$ If spring constant is increased 4 times, PE becomes 4 times. $(B \rightarrow 3)$ (C) Speed of the block, $v=\omega A$ Hence, velocity of the block becomes twice when amplitude of the oscillation is doubled. $(C \rightarrow 2)$ (D) Energy of the oscillation, $E=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} a^{2}$ $E'=\frac{1}{2} m \omega'^{2} a^{2}$ $\Rightarrow E'=\frac{1}{2} m (2\omega)^{2} a^{2}=\frac{4}{2} m \omega^{2} a^{2}$ $(\because)'=2\omega)$ ⇒ E' = 4E Energy of the oscillation becomes 4 times when angular frequency is doubled. $(D \rightarrow 1)$ © examsnet.com

question: A particle of mass $0.4\ \text{kg}$ executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude $0.4\ \text{m}$ . When it passes through the mean position, its kinetic energy is $256 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$ . If the initial phase of the oscillation is $\frac{\pi}{4}$ , then the equation of its motion is _______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given, mass of the particle, $m = 0.4\ \text{kg}$ Amplitude, $A = 0.4\ \text{m}$ Initial phase, $\phi = \frac{\pi}{4}$ Kinetic energy at mean position KE $= 256 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$ As, $KE = \frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} A^{2}$ where, $\omega$ is angular frequency. $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} A^{2} = 256 \times 10^{-3}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times \omega^{2} \times (0.4)^{2} = 256 \times 10^{-3}$ $\Rightarrow \omega^{2} = 8$ $\Rightarrow \omega = 2\sqrt{2}\ \text{rad}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ Equation of simple harmonic motion is given by $x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$ $= 0.4 \sin \left[ (2\sqrt{2}) t + \frac{\pi}{4} \right]$ © examsnet.com

question: Work done in raising a body of mass ' $m$ ' from the surface of the earth to a height $\frac{R}{3}$ is _______. (Where $R$ is radius of earth, $M$ is mass of the earth and $G$ is gravitational constant)

question: The flow rate of water from a tap of diameter $1.25 \text{ cm}$ is 3 litres per minute. If coefficient of viscosity of water is $10^{-3} \text{ Pa}$ . $\text{s}$ , the nature of flow is _______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Given, diameter of tap, $D=1.25 \text{cm}$ $=1.25 \times 10^{-2} \text{m}$ Density of water, $\rho = 10^{3} \text{kgm}^{-3}$ Coefficient of viscosity, $\eta = 10^{-3} \text{Pa-s}$ Volume of water flowing out per second $Q=3 \text{L/min}$ $=\frac{3 \times 10^{-3}}{60}=5 \times 10^{-3} \text{m}^{3} \text{s}^{-1}$ As, $Q=vA=v \times \frac{\pi D^{2}}{4}$ ⇒ $v=\frac{4Q}{D^{2} \pi}$ Reynold's number is given by $R_{r}=\frac{\rho v D}{n}=\frac{4 \rho Q}{\pi D \eta}=\frac{4 \times 10^{3} \times 5 \times 10^{-5}}{314 \times 1.25 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^{-3}}$ = 5095 For Reynold's number, the flow of liquid is turbulent if $R_{c}>3000$ . question: A cylindrical tank is filled with water to a level of $3\ \text{m}$ . A hole is opened at a height of $52.5\ \text{cm}$ from the bottom. The ratio of the area of the hole to that of the cross-sectional area of the tank is $0.1$ . The square of the speed with which water will be coming out from the orifice is ______ $(g=10\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2})$

From equation of continuity, $a v_{e}=Av \Rightarrow v=\frac{a v_{e}}{A}$ Using Bernoulli's theorem, $p_{0}+h\rho g+\frac{1}{2}\rho v^{2}=p_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\rho v_{e'}^{2}$ $\Rightarrow h\rho g+\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(\frac{a v_{c}}{A}\right)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\rho v_{e}^{2}$ or $v_{e}^{2}=\frac{2 g h}{1-\frac{a^{2}}{A^{2}}}=\frac{2 \times (3-0.525) \times 10}{1-(01)^{2}}$ ⇒ $v_{e}^{2}=50\ \text{m}^{2}\ \text{s}^{-2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A wall has two layers $A$ and $B$ , each made of different materials. Both layers are of same thickness. But. the thermal conductivity of material $A$ is twice that of $B$ . If, in the steady state, the temperature difference across the wall is $24^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , then the temperature difference across the layer $B$ is:

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Let $K_{A}$ and $K_{B}$ be the thermal conductivity of material A and B, respectively. Let $T_{1}$ be the temperature of A and $T_{2}$ be the temperature of B. At steady state, rate of flow of heat is given by, $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta Q_{A}}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta Q_{B}}{\Delta t}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{K' A(T_{2}-T_{1})}{l_{A}+l_{B}} = \frac{K_{A} A(T-T_{1})}{l_{A}}$ $= \frac{K_{B} A(T_{2}-T)}{l_{B}}$ ...(i) where K is thermal conductivity of both material and A and l are area and length of the material respectively. Using Eq. (i), we get $\frac{K_{A} A}{l_{A}} (T-T_{1}) = \frac{K_{B} A(T_{2}-T)}{l_{B}}$ ⇒ $2 K_{B} (T-T_{1}) = K_{B} (T_{2}-T)$ $(\because l_{A}=l_{B}$ and $K_{A}=2 K_{B})$ ⇒ $2 T - 2 T_{1} = T_{2} - T$ ⇒ $3 T = T_{2} + 2 T_{1}$ $\Rightarrow T = \frac{2T_{1}+T_{2}}{3}$ Again using Eq. (i). we get $\frac{K' A(T_{2}-T_{1})}{l_{A}+l_{A}} = \frac{K_{A} A(T-T_{1})}{l_{A}}$ ⇒ $\frac{K' (T_{2}-T_{1})}{2 J_{A}} = \frac{K_{A} \left( \frac{2 T_{1}+T_{2}}{3} - T_{1} \right)}{I_{A}}$ ⇒ $\frac{K' (T_{2}-T_{1})}{2} = \frac{K_{A} (T_{2}-T_{1})}{3}$ ⇒ $K' = \frac{2}{3} K_{A} = \frac{2}{3} \times 2 K_{2}$ ⇒ $K' = \frac{4}{3} K_{a}$ Using Eq. (i) to evaluate $(T_{2} - T)$ , $\frac{K' A(T_{2}-T_{1})}{l_{A}+l_{B}} = \frac{K_{B} A(T_{2}-T)}{l_{B}}$ ⇒ $\frac{K' A(T_{2}-T_{1})}{2 l_{A}} = \frac{K_{B} A(T_{2}-T)}{l_{A}}$ ⇒ $\left( \frac{4}{3} K_{B} \right) \frac{A(T_{2}-T_{1})}{2} = K_{B} A(T_{2}-T)$ ⇒ $\frac{2}{3} (T_{2}-T_{1}) = T_{2} - T$ ⇒ $T_{2} - T = \frac{2}{3} (T_{2} - T_{1}) = \frac{2}{3} \times 24^{\circ} = 16^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two circular coils 1 and 2 are made from the same wire. The radius of the $1^{\text{st }}$ coil is twice that of the second coil. What is the ratio of potential difference applied across them $\frac{V_1}{V_2}$ so that the magnetic field at their centers is the same?

question: The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of two particles $A$ and $B$ is $2: 1$ . If the velocities of $A$ and $B$ are $0.05\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ and $0.02\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$ , respectively, then the ratio of their masses $m_{A}: m_{B}$ must be _______

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: According to de-Broglie's wavelength, $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$ Now, de-Broglic's wavelength of particle A is $\lambda_{A} = \frac{h}{m_{A} v_{A}}$ Similarly, de-Broglie's wavelength of particle B is $\lambda_{A} = \frac{h}{m_{B} v_{B}}$ ∴ Ratio of de-Broglic wavelength of A and B is $2: 1$ i.e., $\frac{\lambda_{A}}{\lambda_{B}} = \frac{h}{m_{A} V_{A}} \times \frac{m_{B} v_{B}}{h}$ $\frac{2}{1} = \frac{h}{m_{A} \times 0.05} \times \frac{m_{B} \times 0.02}{h}$ $\frac{2}{1} = \frac{m_{B} \times 0.02}{m_{A} \times 0.05}$ $\frac{2}{0.02} = \frac{m_{B}}{m_{A} \times 0.05}$ $\frac{1}{0.01} = \frac{m_{A}}{m_{B} \times 0.05}$ ⇒ $\frac{m_{A}}{m_{B}} = \frac{1}{5}$ Hence, the ratio of their masses $m_{A}: m_{B}$ is $1: 5$ . © examsnet.com

question: The angle between circles $x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x+4 y+1=0$ and $x^{2}+y^{2}-2 x+6 y-3=0$ is:

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution Standard form of ellipse, $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ ...(i) a > b ∵ Distance between foci $=2 a e$ $2=2 a e$ ⇒ ae  = 1 and length of latusrectum $=\frac{2 b^{2}}{a}$ $\frac{15}{2}=\frac{2 b^{2}}{a}$ $\Rightarrow b^{2}=\frac{15 a}{4}$ ∵ $b^{2}=a^{2}(-e^{2}+1)=-a^{2} e^{2}+a^{2}$ $\frac{15 a}{4}=-1+a^{2}$ ⇒ $4 a^{2}-15 a-4=0$ $4 a^{2}-16 a+a-4=0$ $4 a(a-4)+(a-4)=0$ $(4 a+1)(a-4)=0$ ⇒ $a=-\frac{1}{4}$ and 4 When, $a=+4$ ⇒ $b^{2}=\frac{15 a}{4}=\frac{15 \times 4}{4}$ $\Rightarrow b=\sqrt{15}$ ∴ Equation of ellipse, $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{y^{2}}{15}=1$ ⇒ $15 x^{2}+16 y^{2}=240$ © examsnet.com

question: If the latus rectum subtends a right angle at center of the hyperbola, then its eccentricity is:

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution Given, latus rectum of hyperbola subtends $90^{\circ}$ at its centre. Let there be a hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ ...(i) So, eccentricity, $e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}$ End points of latusrectum are $L=\left(a e, \frac{b^{2}}{a}\right)$ and $L'=\left(a e, -\frac{b^{2}}{a}\right)$ Centre $=(0,0)$ ∵ $\angle LCL'=90^{\circ}$ Then, in $\Delta LCL'$ , by using Pythagoras theorem, $(LC)^{2}+(L'C)^{2}=(LL')^{2}$ $(ae)^{2}+\left(\frac{b^{2}}{a}\right)^{2}+(ae)^{2}+\left(-\frac{b^{2}}{a}\right)^{2}$ $=\left(\frac{2b^{2}}{a}\right)^{2}$ $2\left(a^{2}e^{2}+\frac{b^{4}}{a^{2}}\right)=\frac{4b^{4}}{a^{2}}$ $\Rightarrow \frac{2b^{4}}{a^{2}}=2a^{2}e^{2}$ ⇒ $b^{4}=a^{4}e^{2}$ $[a^{2}(e^{2}-1)]^{2}=a^{4}e^{2}$ $\{\because b^{2}=a^{2}(e^{2}-1)\}$ $a^{4}(e^{2}-1)^{2}=a^{4}e^{2}$ ⇒ $(e^{2}-1)^{2}=e^{2}$ $\Rightarrow e^{2}-1=\pm e$ ⇒ $e^{2}\neq e-1=0$ ⇒ $e=\frac{\pm 1 \pm \sqrt{1+4}}{2}=\frac{\pm1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$ ∵ $e$ can't be negative, hence $e=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: Moment of inertia of a disc of radius ' $R$ ' about a diametric axis is $25\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{m}^{2}$ . The moment of inertia of the disc about a parallel axis at a distance ' $\frac{R}{2}$ ' from the centre is _____

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: From the perpendicular axis theorem, we have $I_{2}=I_{x}+I_{y}$ where, $I_{2}$ is moment of inertia about Z-axis, $I_{x}$ is moment of inertia about X-axis and $I_{y}$ is moment of inertia about Y-axis. Moment of inertia of a disc, $I_{x}=\frac{1}{2} M R^{2}$ Now, $I_{x}=I_{y}$ , because two perpendicular diameters are equivalent. So, $I_{\mathrm{diameter}}=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} M R^{2} = \frac{M R^{2}}{4}$ ⇒ $\frac{M R^{2}}{4}=25$ (given) ⇒ $M=\frac{100}{R^{2}}\ \mathrm{kg}$ Also every diameter passes through centre of mass. So, $I_{\mathrm{COM}}=\frac{M R^{2}}{4}=25\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{m}^{2}$ Using parallel axis theorem, $I=I_{\mathrm{COM}}+M x^{2}$ (where, $.x=\frac{R}{2}$ ) $=25+M\frac{R^{2}}{4}$ $=25+\frac{100}{R^{2}} \times \frac{R^{2}}{4}$ $=50\ \mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{m}^{2}$ © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Efficiency of Carnot engine, $\eta = \frac{1}{5}$ Work done on the system, $W = 50\,\mathrm{J}$ Coefficient of performance of a refrigerator. $\beta = \frac{1-\eta}{\eta}$ $= \frac{1-\frac{1}{5}}{\frac{1}{5}} = \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{5}{1} = 4$ Also, $\beta = \frac{\text{Heat absorbed from reservoir}}{\text{Work done}}$ ⇒ $\beta = \frac{Q}{50}$ ⇒ $4 \times 50 = Q$ ⇒ $Q = 200\,\mathrm{J}$ © examsnet.com
